purpose: Direction checks for the exercise and bone-medication effects. The primary papers' per-site tables were not openly accessible, so effect sizes are NOT fitted; only the direction of benefit is checked.

studies.citation: Smith SM, Heer MA, Shackelford LC, Sibonga JD, Ploutz-Snyder L, Zwart SR. J Bone Miner Res 2012;27(9):1896-1906
studies.population: 13 ISS crewmembers, 2006-2009, 4- to 6-month missions: 8 with iRED, 5 with ARED
quotes: Of these 13, 8 had access to the iRED and 5 had access to the ARED.

Bone densitometry revealed significant interactions (time and exercise device) for pelvis bone mineral density (BMD) and bone mineral content (p < 0.01), hip femoral neck BMD (p < 0.05), trochanter BMD (p < 0.05), and total hip BMD (p < 0.05).
These variables were unchanged from preflight only for ARED crewmembers, who also returned from flight with higher percent lean mass and lower percent fat mass.

studies.citation: LeBlanc A, et al. Osteoporos Int 2013;24(7):2105-2114
studies.access: Not openly accessible; finding taken from the open review below

secondary_source.citation: Rosenthal R, et al. The Case for Bisphosphonate Use in Astronauts Flying Long-Duration Missions. Cells 2024
quotes: improved resistance training with ARED exercise attenuates previously observed declines in DXA-measured bone mineral density after the usual 6-month missions
The combined therapies (ARED + BP) were associated with significant attenuation or complete protection in postflight aBMD of crewmembers compared with those who used only ARED alone.

not_established: How many minutes of exercise produce how much benefit, and the size of the medication effect. Next step: obtain the full text (Smith 2012 Table 3; LeBlanc 2013 Table 2) and fit countermeasure_max_effect.
